This is the shape *this* project gave the record machinery: the document
families it named, where entries are filed, where views are rendered, and what
to type to add one. It is a description of `luria.yaml` as configured, not of
what `luria.yaml` can hold — for the key-by-key schema, with defaults and
meanings, see [Luria's configuration reference](https://github.com/dmarx/luria/blob/main/docs/configuration.md).

## Referable documents

A code — `ADR-012` — resolves to a document, and every reference to it in this repository is checked. `luria lint` fails on a bare code that was never linked; `luria link --fix` writes the link so nobody has to know where the document renders.

| a code looks like | filed in | rendered to | in force when status is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LIT-001` | `record/literature.d/` | `docs/literature/README.md` + tag pages | `Active` |
| `NOTE-001` | `record/notes.d/` | `docs/notes/README.md` + tag pages | `Read` |
| `THEORY-001` | `record/theory.d/` | `docs/theory/README.md` + tag pages | `Active` |
| `ADR-001` | `record/decisions.d/` | `docs/decisions/README.md` + tag pages | `Active` |
| `DP-001` | `record/principles.d/` | `docs/design-principles.md` (one page, read as a whole) | `Active` |
| `QUESTION-001` | `record/questions.d/` | `docs/questions/README.md` + tag pages | `Open` |
| `CLAIM-001` | `record/claims.d/` | `docs/claims/README.md` + tag pages | `Active` |
| `CASE-001` | `record/cases.d/` | `docs/cases/README.md` + tag pages | `Active` |

## What each family is

A scheme's own account of itself, where it gives one — `title` and `blurb` on `schemes.X`. The table above says where a family's files live and how its codes are spelled; this says what the family is for, which is the part a reader needs first and the part a config could not previously state (#279).


## What an entry must carry

Every entry carries `title` and `date`. Everything else is listed below rather than assumed: `status` and the axis are controlled fields the scheme declares, and every relation — the successor a retiring document names included — is a reference the scheme declares, with the conditions it states (ADR-071, ADR-125). What each scheme's entries must carry, compiled from `luria.yaml` into the contract `luria lint` checks, with where each obligation was declared. A finding cites the same line.

**`LIT`**

- `extends` — optional, one or more `LIT` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.LIT.references.extends) — *the earlier paper this one builds on and could not stand without. Papers fork where the DESIGNS differ, practices where the RECOMMENDATIONS do, so a fork can exist at one layer and not the other (ADR-011).*
- `extended_by` — optional, one or more `LIT` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.LIT.references.extended_by) — *the converse of `extends`, written by `luria link --fix`.*
- `compared_against` — optional, one or more `LIT` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.LIT.references.compared_against) — *this paper evaluated itself against that one. Somebody ran the comparison; a shared topic is not one (ADR-011).*
- `corrects` — optional, one or more `LIT` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.LIT.references.corrects) — *this paper shows the earlier one wrong on something it claimed. Retire by status, never by deletion — the body stays.*
- `rivals` — optional, one or more `LIT` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.LIT.references.rivals) — *this paper argues for an account of the same phenomenon that the other paper's account excludes, and neither tests or corrects the other. Settled, it becomes `corrects` on the winner (ADR-022).*
- `corrected_by` — optional, one or more `LIT` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.LIT.references.corrected_by) — *the converse of `corrects`, written by `luria link --fix`.*
- `supports` — optional, one or more `CLAIM` or `ARG` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.LIT.references.supports) — *the record's own claims and arguments that rest on this work without a reading of it, written by `luria link --fix` from their `grounds`. A THEORY drawn from the work is the stronger footing*
- `superseded_by` — required when `status` is `Superseded`, one or more `LIT` or `ANTH` codes when present; forbidden when `status` is `Active` (luria.yaml: schemes.LIT.references.superseded_by)
- `status` — optional, one of `Active`, `Proposed`, `Deferred`, `Superseded`, `Rejected` (luria.yaml: schemes.LIT.fields.status; vocabulary 'lit-statuses': values) — *A work's standing in this record: whether it is worth reading. Not whether its findings are true — that is the THEORY scheme's business, and the two can disagree in either direction.*
- `tags` — required, one or more of `quantum-foundations`, `contextuality`, `mathematics`, `game-theory`, `network-science`, `complex-systems`, `probabilistic-modeling`, `neuroscience`, `natural-sciences`, `ecology`, `thermodynamics`, `operations-research`, `society-and-governance`, `information-theory`, `representation-learning`, `learning-theory`, `compositionality`, `mathematical-statistics`, `information-retrieval`, `design-rationale`, `social-science`, `causality`, `pragmatics`, `myth-and-folklore`, `translation`, `linguistics`, `metaphysics`, `mereology`, `agency`, `individuation`, `self`, `personhood`, `behavioral-integration`, `phenomenal-unity`, `narrative-unity`, `self-governance`, `phenomenology`, `social-ontology`, `moral-psychology`, `psychopathology-and-treatment`, `motivation`, `well-being`, `learning-and-conditioning`, `psychometrics`, `philosophy-of-biology`, `embodied-cognition`, `free-will`, `model-comparison`, `information-geometry`, `loss-landscapes`, `ethics`, `consciousness`, `cognition`, `emotion-and-affect`, `philosophy-of-science`, `epistemology`, `logic`, `philosophy-of-mathematics`, `philosophy-of-language`, `religion`, `anthology-candidate` (luria.yaml: schemes.LIT.fields.tags; vocabulary 'topics': values) — *What a work is about. - `primary_topic` — derived — `{tags[0]}`, never written (luria.yaml: schemes.LIT.fields.primary_topic)

**`NOTE`**

- `paper` — required, a `LIT` code (luria.yaml: schemes.NOTE.references.paper) — *the paper this note is a close reading of. Absence of a note means the paper is unread (ADR-025).*

**`THEORY`**

- `source` — required, one or more `LIT` codes (luria.yaml: schemes.THEORY.references.source) — *the work this account comes from. Same test as a practice's: what the explanation could not survive losing.*
- `extends` — optional, one or more `THEORY` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.THEORY.references.extends) — *the earlier account this one builds on — a refinement or a widening of the same mechanism, not a rival one.*
- `extended_by` — optional, one or more `THEORY` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.THEORY.references.extended_by) — *the converse of `extends`, written by `luria link --fix`.*
- `rivals` — optional, one or more `THEORY` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.THEORY.references.rivals) — *another account of the same phenomenon that cannot also be right, where neither yet corrects the other. Settled, it becomes `corrects` on the winner and a status on the loser (ADR-022).*
- `corrects` — optional, one or more `THEORY` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.THEORY.references.corrects) — *this account replaces the earlier one's reasoning. What the old account explained may still happen; only the reason was wrong.*
- `corrected_by` — optional, one or more `THEORY` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.THEORY.references.corrected_by) — *the converse of `corrects`, written by `luria link --fix`.*
- `presupposes` — optional, one or more `THEORY` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.THEORY.references.presupposes) — *this account takes the other's conclusion as a premise for a claim about something else. If the other falls, this one loses a premise and needs another route; it is not a refinement of the same mechanism, which is `extends` (ADR-029).*
- `presupposed_by` — optional, one or more `THEORY` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.THEORY.references.presupposed_by) — *the converse of `presupposes`, written by `luria link --fix`.*
- `answers` — optional, one or more `QUESTION` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.THEORY.references.answers) — *a question of the record's own that this account answers, so the question's page shows the literature beside the record's claims (ADR-032)*
- `supports` — optional, one or more `CLAIM` or `ARG` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.THEORY.references.supports) — *the record's own claims and arguments resting on this account, written by `luria link --fix` from their `grounds`. Rejecting this account leaves each of them needing another route*

**`CLAIM`**

- `answers` — optional, one or more `QUESTION` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.CLAIM.references.answers) — *the question this claim is an answer to*

- `undercuts` — optional, one or more `ARG` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.CLAIM.references.undercuts) — *the argument whose inference this claim denies, leaving its premises and its conclusion standing*

- `supersedes` — optional, one or more `CLAIM` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.CLAIM.references.supersedes) — *the claim this one replaced, written by `luria link --fix` from its `superseded_by`*
- `complements` — optional, one or more `CLAIM` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.CLAIM.references.complements) — *answers a different part of the same question, so the two belong together rather than competing. **`CASE`**

- `supports` — optional, one or more `CLAIM` or `ARG` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.CASE.references.supports) — *the claims and arguments grounded in this case, written by `luria link --fix` from their `grounds`.*
- `illustrates` — optional, one or more `CLAIM` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.CASE.references.illustrates) — *a claim this case makes vivid without bearing its weight. Losing the case costs the claim an example, not a premise; that is what separates this from `grounds`*
- `counterexample_to` — optional, one or more `CLAIM` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.CASE.references.counterexample_to) — *a claim this case shows false as stated*
- `variant_of` — optional, one or more `CASE` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.CASE.references.variant_of) — *the case this one alters in a stated respect, as Northstar-B alters Northstar-A*
- `variants` — optional, one or more `CASE` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.CASE.references.variants) — *the converse of `variant_of`, written by `luria link --fix`.*
- `substitutes_for` — optional, one or more `CASE` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.CASE.references.substitutes_for) — *the case this one replaces in the argument — usually a fictional company standing in for a real one, so the argument does not ride on contested facts about it*
- `substituted_by` — optional, one or more `CASE` codes when present (luria.yaml: schemes.CASE.references.substituted_by) — *the converse of `substitutes_for`, written by `luria link --fix`.*
- `superseded_by` — required when `status` is `Superseded`, one or more `CASE` codes when present; forbidden when `status` is `Active` (luria.yaml: schemes.CASE.references.superseded_by)

## Journals

Dated observations. An entry is true about the day it was written and is never revised or consumed — the books are a view over sources that stay, which is what makes a journal safe to write into without coordinating.

| journal | entries filed at | books rendered to | one book per | titled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `curation` | `record/curation.d/` `yyyy/mm/dd/hhmmss.md` | `docs/curation/` | month | Curation log |
| `workbench` | `record/workbench.d/` `yyyy/mm/dd/hhmmss.md` | `docs/workbench/` | month | Workbench |
| `devlog` | `record/devlog.d/` `yyyy/mm/dd/hhmmss.md` | `docs/devlog/` | month | Development log |

## Fragment directories

One file per contribution, assembled into a single document and then consumed. The point is the absence of a shared file to conflict on: every contributor writes a new path.

| directory | assembled into | style |
|---|---|---|
| `record/changelog.d/` | `CHANGELOG.md` | append |

## Other projects this record cites

A prefixed code reaches into another project's record, so a citation says whose decision it is at the point of use rather than leaving the reader to guess.

## Filing something new

Every kind this project scaffolds, straight from the dispatch table `luria new` itself uses.

| command | files |
|---|---|
| `luria new --kind adr --title "…"` | a document in the `ADR` scheme, numbered for you |
| `luria new --kind arg --title "…"` | a document in the `ARG` scheme, numbered for you |
| `luria new --kind case --title "…"` | a document in the `CASE` scheme, numbered for you |
| `luria new --kind changelog --title "…"` | a fragment in `record/changelog.d/` |
| `luria new --kind claim --title "…"` | a document in the `CLAIM` scheme, numbered for you |
| `luria new --kind curation --title "…"` | a dated entry in the `curation` journal |
| `luria new --kind devlog --title "…"` | a dated entry in the `devlog` journal |
| `luria new --kind dp --title "…"` | a document in the `DP` scheme, numbered for you |
| `luria new --kind lit --title "…"` | a document in the `LIT` scheme, numbered for you |
| `luria new --kind migration --title "…"` | a migration spec |
| `luria new --kind note --title "…"` | a document in the `NOTE` scheme, numbered for you |
| `luria new --kind question --title "…"` | a document in the `QUESTION` scheme, numbered for you |
| `luria new --kind term --title "…"` | a document in the `TERM` scheme, numbered for you |
| `luria new --kind theory --title "…"` | a document in the `THEORY` scheme, numbered for you |
| `luria new --kind workbench --title "…"` | a dated entry in the `workbench` journal |
